details:
Mission Architect is an interactive space mission design and simulation game that allows players to experience the challenges of planning a space mission. Players begin by selecting a mission and its destination, then assemble a spacecraft by choosing components and instruments while managing constraints such as budget, mass, power, launch capacity, and mission requirements.

After completing spacecraft assembly, players launch and simulate their missions, where their design decisions influence the outcome. The game features two difficulty levels. Normal Mode focuses on completing the selected mission, while Hard Mode adds the challenge of landing safely on the selected planetary destination. This requires players to consider their spacecraft design and prepare for the additional demands of landing.

The main benefit of Mission Architect is that it makes space mission planning more accessible and engaging. Players can experiment with different spacecraft designs, observe the consequences of their decisions, and develop a better understanding of engineering trade-offs.

Our intended impact is to encourage interest in space science, aerospace engineering, and problem-solving, particularly among students and people curious about space exploration.

The project was developed using Rust as the programming language and Macroquad as the game framework. It is hosted online through Vercel, allowing users to access it through a web browser.

What makes Mission Architect creative is its combination of spacecraft design, resource management, and interactive mission simulation. Our team considered factors such as mission objectives, spacecraft configuration, budget limits, mass, power availability, launch constraints, and the additional challenges involved in planetary landing.
